validated: On curved SubD surfaces, equal polygon count does not substitute for even spacing and balanced flow.
Candidate pinch count cannot be optimized in isolation; the matched curved failure had fewer candidates but worse severity/median curvature and a less balanced visible arc.
A continuous local perimeter support ring can redirect the interior grid away from a boundary and sharpen the resulting highlight.
Support density has a measurable cost and should follow edge function rather than being added globally.
A 2-to-1 reduction must keep every quad convex/outward; moving one reduction vertex behind the incoming boundary can remain numerically all-quad/manifold after evaluation yet create an obvious pinch.
not_yet_validated: different-geometry transfer of the loop-termination rule
